Search and AI answers, measured 13 September 2026

Where dmp.com stands, and what it is worth to fix

The search and AI-answer numbers come from a Semrush pull on 13 September 2026 and nine buyer searches run from Springfield, Missouri. The page-level numbers come from an audit of 241 public pages on www.dmp.com on 9 November 2026: the home page, the pages, the product categories and a sample of product pages. A correction to the September report: that crawl started at the redirecting apex and could read one URL, so its findings about the home page's title, H1, canonical, robots.txt, sitemap and structured data were wrong for the real site. They are replaced here. This is the baseline we measure against at 30, 60 and 90 days.

Readiness on sixteen checks, every page: the site today against the build, scored by the same script.

7,462organic keywords, but 66 percent of the traffic is branded
24,493organic visits a month, worth $247,680 a month in paid equivalent
0 of 9top-ten appearances for the buyer searches asked from Springfield
39Authority Score, against 60 at vivint.com, 55 at safehome.org and 24 at barcomsecurity.com

Top findings

Ranked by what they cost, with the fix

Each finding carries its evidence, what it costs today, and what the build or the 90-day plan does about it.

2 critical6 high3 medium2 low
1
Critical

DMP does not appear in the top ten for a single buyer search asked from its own city

Evidence
Nine searches were run from Springfield, Missouri and dmp.com is absent from all nine top-ten lists. barcomsecurity.com holds position 1 for 'commercial security system springfield' and appears in five of the nine, passfireandsecurity.com in five, centralillinoissecurity.com in five, safehome.org in six and vivint.com in five. The terms that carry demand are small but easy: 'commercial security system springfield' is 90 a month at difficulty 1, 'video surveillance system springfield' 90 a month at difficulty 0, 'access control system springfield' 20 a month at difficulty 0, 'alarm monitoring springfield' 10 a month at difficulty 0. The other four have no Semrush entry, which puts them under about 10 a month.
What it costs
Every buyer, specifier and installer searching security in Springfield lands on a competitor or on a page about Springfield Illinois, Ohio or Tennessee. DMP is headquartered in the city and is not in the conversation for a set of terms whose difficulty scores are 0 and 1.
What we do
Build one Springfield, Missouri page at /springfield-missouri/ covering the headquarters, the product lines and the local dealer list, titled for the city and the state so the engines stop confusing it with the other Springfields. In the build.
2
Critical

Named in none of the AI answers about security in Springfield

Evidence
Six questions were put to Claude with web search from Springfield, Missouri on 13 September 2026. Four returned an answer and two timed out. DMP was named in 0 and cited in 0. The sources the engine read instead were barcomsecurity.com in three answers, expertise.com in three, and atlassecurity.com, georgealarm.com, securitymonster.com, springfieldalarmcompany.com and vivint.com in two each.
What it costs
When someone asks an assistant who supplies intrusion, access control or monitoring in Springfield, the answer is assembled from other companies' pages and from directories DMP has no profile on. That is a channel where the brand simply does not exist.
What we do
The same body of work that fixes the search results: a Springfield page, eight system pages written in buyers' words, and the markup the site lacks today (LocalBusiness, Product, FAQPage and sameAs) so an engine has something to read and attribute. In the build.
3
High

The front door takes three hops, and robots.txt answers 404

Evidence
https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which then answers 307, a temporary redirect, rather than one permanent redirect to https. https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although the file holds rules and two Sitemap lines; crawlers treat a 4xx robots file as no file, so the rules and the sitemap declaration are never read. The XML sitemap itself is live at /sitemaps-1-sitemap.xml and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages, and a second Sitemap line points at a gforce.www.dmp.com host.
What it costs
Search engines and AI crawlers that start at the apex or over http make extra hops, one of them temporary, and the file meant to steer them and declare the sitemap is ignored. DMP's crawl policy is whatever the 404 implies, not a decision.
What we do
Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200, declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers and drop the gforce line. In the build, week one.
4
High

Organization markup exists, but nothing describes the products, the questions or the profiles

Evidence
Of 241 pages audited, 226 carry Organization, WebPage and BreadcrumbList markup with the address, phone number and founding date. None carries Product, ItemList, FAQPage or LocalBusiness markup, none has a sameAs link, and none declares a contact point (0 of 241), although DMP publishes four support lines with hours. The most specific type on a product page is WebPage. vivint.com's Springfield page carries Organization, Service, PostalAddress, GeoCoordinates and ContactPoint; safehome.org's carries Organization, LocalBusiness, PostalAddress, ItemList and BreadcrumbList.
What it costs
Search engines and answer engines know who DMP is and where it is, but not what the 369 products are, which questions they answer or which LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase profiles belong to the company, so they fall back on Indeed, Glassdoor and Reddit for the brand and on distributors for the products.
What we do
Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages, a ContactPoint for each support line, LocalBusiness for the headquarters and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. In the build.
5
High

Two thirds of the traffic is people who already know the brand

Evidence
Semrush puts branded share at 66 percent. The top organic term is 'dmp' at 9,900 a month, holding 32.33 percent of all traffic on its own, followed by 'digital monitoring products' at 880 and a long list of part numbers: 'dmp xr150' 390, 'dmp keypad' 390, 'dmp xr550' 260, 'dmp 734' 210. The one high-volume non-branded term in the top thirty is 'white on white paper' at 12,100 a month, position 9, which lands on the JamAlert white paper and has nothing to do with security.
What it costs
The site harvests existing dealers and customers looking up model numbers and support logins. It does not introduce DMP to anyone who has not already heard the name, so the whole top of the funnel depends on trade shows, reps and word of mouth.
What we do
Build the eight system pages and a resource hub that target category language rather than part numbers, starting with access control and fire. In the build for the pages, 90-day plan for the content programme.
6
High

The catalogue is built by part number, with no page written for the buyer's own search words

Evidence
dmp.com organises its catalogue by product category (26 categories) and by part number (369 product pages). No page is written for the phrase a buyer types. Semrush shows the top-ranking pages are individual SKUs such as /products/control-panels/xr-series/xr150 and /products/access-control/modules/734, while 'access control systems' (9,900 a month) and 'fire detection and fire alarm system' (6,600) go to distributors and integrators.
What it costs
A buyer who searches 'access control systems' meets a part number page written for someone who already chose the part, so the searches go to distributors and integrators instead.
What we do
Build a page for each system line (intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators, wireless, panels and keypads, Virtual Keypad and software), each with question headings, FAQPage markup and links down to the products. In the build.
7
High

The brand reputation result is owned by job boards and Reddit

Evidence
The search 'digital monitoring products reviews', run from Springfield, returns indeed.com at 1, glassdoor.com at 2 and a r/springfieldMO thread at 3 titled 'I can't recommend anyone work for DMP'. Positions 4 to 10 are simplyhired.com, a second glassdoor.com result, facebook.com, a second indeed.com result, ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com. dmp.com appears nowhere on the page.
What it costs
Anyone checking DMP out before specifying it, and any AI answer summarising the brand, reads employment complaints first because the company publishes nothing that answers the question. No Review or AggregateRating markup exists anywhere on the site to compete.
What we do
Publish an about and proof page carrying dealer testimonials, installation case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and every service page. In the 30-day plan.
8
High

Nothing on the site answers a question in the words buyers use

Evidence
Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none carries FAQPage markup. Semrush records real question demand across the lines: 'how to turn off fire alarm system' 720 a month, 'how to reset fire alarm system' 320, 'what is access control system' 210, 'what is fire alarm system' 210, 'what is the best home video surveillance system' 210, 'what is a central station fire alarm system' 170. None of the four Springfield competitors carries FAQPage markup either.
What it costs
These are exactly the phrasings answer engines lift from. Because nobody in this set has claimed them, the ground is open and DMP is choosing not to stand on it.
What we do
Put six to eight questions with direct answers and FAQPage markup at the foot of each of the eight system pages, drawn from the question lists above. In the build for the markup, 30-day plan for the copy.
9
Medium

Pages say little about what they are: short titles, one shared description, thin copy, images without alt text

Evidence
Of 241 pages audited, 66 have a title under 25 characters (usually the part name and 'DMP.com'), 107 share one default meta description, 175 have fewer than 300 words (median 174) and 226 have at least one image with no alt attribute. 137 use the same default Open Graph image. The home page is the strongest page at 52 of 100, and no page scores above a D. 15 pages returned an unusual response during the crawl (title 'POST data') and need a re-check, so they are left out of these counts.
What it costs
A title like 'XT75 | DMP.com' does not say what the product is, so a search result or an AI summary cannot tell a panel from a keypad. Shared descriptions and thin copy give engines nothing to quote, and missing alt text is an accessibility failure on almost every page.
What we do
Generate a descriptive title, a unique description, alt text and 300 or more words from the product table for every product page, and give shared links a product image. In the build.
10
Medium

The category head terms are all unranked, and the reachable ones are being ignored

Evidence
DMP holds no position for any of the ten highest-volume terms in its categories: 'security camera' 550,000 a month, 'adt' 246,000, 'diy home security systems' 135,000, 'best home security cameras' 110,000, 'home security systems' 74,000. Semrush values reaching position 3 on that set at 173,873 clicks a month and $1,063,192 a month in paid equivalent. Those are consumer terms at difficulty 46 to 79 and the outlook on every one is long haul, but the commercial terms are within reach of an Authority Score of 39: 'access control systems' 9,900 at difficulty 58, 'fire detection and fire alarm system' 6,600 at 42, 'smart smoke detector' 6,600 at 35, 'access control companies' 1,600 at 29, 'door access control systems' 1,600 at 22.
What it costs
There is no pipeline of non-branded demand at all, and the winnable commercial terms are being left to distributors while the unwinnable consumer terms are quoted as the target.
What we do
Point the access control and fire pages at the difficulty 22 to 42 commercial terms and build supporting question pages beneath them. In the 90-day plan.
11
Medium

The backlink total rests on one relationship

Evidence
The profile is 22,880 links from 1,916 referring domains, above the median of 832 across the five competitors measured, and 88.1 percent of the links pass authority. But nationaljeweler.com accounts for 85.3 percent of every link to the site, and 89.7 percent of links, 20,514 of 22,880, are image links carrying no anchor text. Authority Score is 39 against 60 at vivint.com and 55 at safehome.org.
What it costs
The headline link number overstates the real position. If that one relationship or that one site changes, most of the profile goes with it, and image links say nothing about what DMP makes, so they build no topical signal.
What we do
Earn links from domains that have none yet, starting with security trade publications, the Springfield chamber and business press, and dealer sites, and ask partners who link with a logo to put the company name in the alt text. In the 90-day plan.
12
Low

AI crawlers are allowed by accident, not by policy, and llms.txt is not published

Evidence
GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bingbot and Googlebot are all able to read the site, which scores 94 of 100 on AI answer access against 100 at safehome.org. That permission exists because the robots file answers 404 and is ignored, not because a file grants it. llms.txt is not published (the address returns 404).
What it costs
Low today, but the moment anyone adds a default robots.txt the access can disappear without being noticed, and there is no file telling an engine which pages matter.
What we do
Publish a deliberate robots.txt that names and allows the eight crawlers, and an llms.txt listing the home page, the eight system pages, the Springfield page and the support hub. In the build, week one.
13
Low

No paid search at all, and no paid-sourced contacts in the CRM

Evidence
DMP runs 0 ad keywords. HubSpot records 0 contacts from paid search, 0 from paid social and 0 from display in the 90 days since 15 June 2026. vivint.com buys ten of its own brand terms, including 'vivint' at 165,000 a month and $8.05 a click and 'vivint security' at 22,200 a month and $11.90 a click.
What it costs
Nothing is being wasted, but nothing is being defended either. With 'dmp' at 9,900 a month and rising dealer interest, a competitor or a distributor can bid on the brand name at any time and pay very little for it.
What we do
Once the service pages exist, run a small brand-defence campaign on the five brand terms and a test on 'access control companies' and 'door access control systems'. In the 90-day plan.

Highest leverage moves

Five moves, in the order we would make them

The five moves with the biggest return for the least effort, in the order we would do them. Each one is either in the build or in the first 30 days of the plan.

1

Fix the front door: one 301, a working robots.txt, a declared sitemap

Build, week oneIn the build

https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which answers 307, and https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. Serve every address variant with a single permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200 and declare the sitemap in it, name the eight AI crawlers so their access is a decision rather than an accident, publish llms.txt and remove the gforce line. This is the cheapest fix in the report and every other measurement depends on it.

2

Describe the products, the questions and the profiles to machines

Build, weeks one and twoIn the build

Organization markup is already on 226 of 241 pages. Add what is missing: Product markup from the product table on every product page, ItemList on the category pages, FAQPage on the system pages, a ContactPoint for each of the four support lines, LocalBusiness for the Springfield headquarters and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. Vivint's Springfield page carries Organization, Service, PostalAddress, GeoCoordinates and ContactPoint and is cited in two of the four AI answers we captured.

3

Build the Springfield, Missouri page

Build, weeks two and threeIn the build

DMP appears in 0 of 9 top-ten lists asked from Springfield, and the pages beating it are frequently about Springfield Illinois, Ohio or Tennessee. The winnable terms are 'commercial security system springfield' at 90 a month and difficulty 1 and 'video surveillance system springfield' at 90 a month and difficulty 0. Build /springfield-missouri/ with the state in the title, the headquarters story, the eight system lines, the local dealer list, a form and a phone number, and LocalBusiness schema. Barcom holds position 1 on that page type with 1,078 words and no schema at all.

4

Build the system pages with questions answered on them

30 days, marketingIn the 30-day plan

DMP's catalogue is organised by category and part number, and no page is written for the buyer's phrase. Build one page for each system line (intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators, wireless, panels and keypads, Virtual Keypad and software), each 900 words or more with question headings, FAQPage markup, links down to the matching products and an enquiry form. Use the measured question demand: 'how to turn off fire alarm system' 720 a month, 'how to reset fire alarm system' 320, 'what is access control system' 210, 'what is the best home video surveillance system' 210. None of the four Springfield competitors carries FAQPage markup, so this ground is unclaimed.

5

Take back the brand result and start on the reachable commercial terms

90 days, marketing and salesIn the 90-day plan

'digital monitoring products reviews' returns Indeed at 1, Glassdoor at 2 and a Reddit thread criticising DMP as an employer at 3, with dmp.com nowhere in the top ten, and 66 percent of organic traffic is already branded. Publish an about and proof page with dealer testimonials, case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and all eight system pages. At the same time point the access control and fire pages at the commercial terms within reach of an Authority Score of 39: 'access control companies' 1,600 a month at difficulty 29, 'door access control systems' 1,600 at 22, 'smart smoke detector' 6,600 at 35, 'fire detection and fire alarm system' 6,600 at 42. Support both with links from trade press, the Springfield business community and dealer sites, since 85.3 percent of the current profile comes from a single domain.

Entity graph

What the markup says about who you are

Type names alone do not make a page citable. These checks read the graph: which entities the page names, whether they are joined to each other, and whether every reference resolves. That is what an answer engine follows before it will name a company as the answer.

144 of 241pages whose graph scores D or F

The blog

No blog, no insights section, no answers in buyers' words

dmp.com publishes news and updates, case studies, technical updates, spec sheets and white papers, but none is written as the answer to a buyer's question. Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none carries FAQPage markup, and the median page has 174 words. That leaves nothing on the site written in the language a buyer or an AI engine uses when it asks how a system works, what it costs or which type to choose. Semrush does show a white paper URL ranking at position 9 for a 12,100 a month phrase, so long-form material exists, but it is not pointed at the questions people ask.

36 of 241pages with a question heading
174median words per page across the 241 audited pages
0pages with Article schema
0pages with a FAQ block

What we found

  • Publishing is news-led: press releases, personnel announcements, technical updates and case studies. None is written as an answer to a buyer's question.
  • Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none has FAQPage markup, so very little on the site is shaped as an answer.
  • The question demand is real and unclaimed: "how to turn off fire alarm system" at 720 a month, "do it yourself wireless home security systems" at 320, "what is access control system" at 210, "what is the best home video surveillance system" at 210, and "how does access control system work" at 70.
  • Intrusion questions are thinner: "what is intrusion alarm system" is 20 a month and the rest of that set sits under 10, so intrusion content should be written for dealers and specifiers, not for search volume.
  • One resource page, /resources/white-papers/jamalert-white-paper, ranks 9th for "white on white paper" at 12,100 a month, which is accidental traffic from a phrase that has nothing to do with alarms.

What we would do

Build Give the news, case studies and answer pages one index linked from the main navigation, and put Article markup on every post template.

30 days Publish three answer pages tied to the pulled questions: what an access control system is and how it works, how a monitored fire alarm system works, and how to choose a video surveillance system. Each one answers the question in the first fifty words.

60 days Add a FAQ block marked up as FAQPage to each of the eight system pages, using the pulled questions for that line, and link every post to its service line page.

90 days Publish three more posts against the DIY wireless and smart smoke detector questions, and review the jamalert white paper page so the traffic it already earns lands on something relevant.

Social and the entity

Nothing on dmp.com tells a machine who Digital Monitoring Products is

An answer engine decides what a company is from structured data and from the profiles that data points to. DMP's pages already say who the company is, with the address, phone number and founding date in Organization markup. What they do not say is what the products are, which questions they answer, which profiles are the company's, or how to reach each support team. Every machine reading the site has to guess those.

226 of 241pages carrying Organization markup
0 of 241pages with Product, FAQPage or LocalBusiness markup
0 of 241sameAs links to company profiles
1,916referring domains pointing at dmp.com

What we found

  • Organization markup is present on 226 of 241 pages audited, with the address, phone number and founding date. Product, ItemList, FAQPage and LocalBusiness markup are absent everywhere, and the most specific type on a product page is WebPage.
  • There are no sameAs links on any of the 241 pages, so nothing on dmp.com connects the company to its LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB or YouTube entries.
  • No page declares a contact point. DMP publishes four support lines with hours and email addresses, none of them in markup, and there is no Springfield location page.
  • Titles are short, usually the part name and 'DMP.com' (66 of 241 are under 25 characters), and 107 pages share one default description.
  • Authority is not the problem: 1,916 referring domains with an Authority Score of 39, above the median of 832 domains across the five measured competitors. The company is well linked and badly described.

What we would do

Build Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, and give each page a title and description that name the product and the category.

30 days Add Organization and LocalBusiness JSON-LD to the home page with the legal name, the Springfield address, the phone number, the logo and sameAs links to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia.

60 days Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, and FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages.

90 days Claim and complete the Google Business Profile and the BBB and Crunchbase entries so the details match the schema word for word, then add Review markup once first-party reviews are collected.

Where the traffic comes from

Today, in numbers

  • Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,462 organic keywords and 24,493 organic visits a month, valued at 247,680 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running.
  • 66 per cent of that organic traffic comes from people already searching the brand: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month accounts for 32.33 per cent of it.
  • The home page is sound on the basics: a title, one H1, a canonical tag, 628 words, a phone link, a form and Organization markup with the address, phone number and founding date. It still scores 52 of 100, and across 241 public pages the average is 35 and none scores above a D.
  • https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. The XML sitemap is live and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages. The apex takes a 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, then a 307.
  • The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent.
  • 175 of 241 pages have fewer than 300 words, 107 share one default meta description, 66 titles are under 25 characters, 226 pages have an image without alt text, and none carries Product, FAQPage, LocalBusiness or sameAs markup.
  • Asked nine buyer searches from Springfield, Missouri, DMP appeared in the top ten for none of them.
  • Backlinks are strong on paper, 22,880 links from 1,916 domains at Authority Score 39, but 85.3 per cent of the links come from a single domain, nationaljeweler.com, and 89.7 per cent are image links carrying no anchor text.

Local and reviews

What a buyer sees next to the map

  • The query "digital monitoring products reviews", asked from Springfield, Missouri, returns no dmp.com page in the top ten.
  • Indeed holds first place with "Working at Digital Monitoring Products, Inc.: 25 Reviews", an employer review page, not a product one.
  • Glassdoor holds second place and appears twice in the top ten with employer reviews.
  • A Reddit thread in r/springfieldMO sits third, titled "I can't recommend anyone work for DMP".
  • SimplyHired, Facebook and a second Indeed listing take four more of the ten places.
  • The only industry results are ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com, none of them owned or influenced by DMP.
  • No star rating appears in any result title except Indeed's count of 25 reviews, and no review markup was found on dmp.com, so no rating can be shown next to the brand in search.
  • Across the eight service and buyer queries asked from Springfield, Missouri, DMP is absent from all top tens; the ten places are held by passfireandsecurity.com, barcomsecurity.com, centralillinoissecurity.com, eccoinc.com, safehome.org, vivint.com, springfieldalarmcompany.com and others.

The 90-day plan

What happens, in order

Days 1 to 10

Fix the front door. Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200 and declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers, publish llms.txt, and give every page its own title and description.

Days 10 to 45

Build the eight system pages: intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators and monitoring, wireless, panels and keypads, and Virtual Keypad and software. Each gets 800 words or more, H2 sections, a FAQ block marked up as FAQPage using the pulled questions, Service schema, ten or more internal links and an enquiry form.

Days 45 to 60

Build the Springfield, Missouri page with the city in the title, the address, a tappable phone number, a form and links to the eight system pages, and add sameAs links from the home page schema to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia.

Days 60 to 90

Take back the brand result: publish an about page, a careers page and a company news page under dmp.com so branded queries have owned destinations, start collecting first-party reviews, and publish the first three answer posts against the access control, fire alarm and video surveillance questions.

Day 90

Re-run the same nine Springfield searches, the same six AI questions and the same page audit against this baseline, and decide whether to open a small paid search test on the reachable access control terms rather than the 543,664 a month the full national list would cost.

In one list

  1. DMP does not appear in the top ten for a single buyer search asked from its own city. Build one Springfield, Missouri page at /springfield-missouri/ covering the headquarters, the product lines and the local dealer list, titled for the city and the state so the engines stop confusing it with the other Springfields. In the build.
  2. Named in none of the AI answers about security in Springfield. The same body of work that fixes the search results: a Springfield page, eight system pages written in buyers' words, and the markup the site lacks today (LocalBusiness, Product, FAQPage and sameAs) so an engine has something to read and attribute. In the build.
  3. The front door takes three hops, and robots.txt answers 404. Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200, declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers and drop the gforce line. In the build, week one.
  4. Organization markup exists, but nothing describes the products, the questions or the profiles. Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages, a ContactPoint for each support line, LocalBusiness for the headquarters and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. In the build.
  5. Two thirds of the traffic is people who already know the brand. Build the eight system pages and a resource hub that target category language rather than part numbers, starting with access control and fire. In the build for the pages, 90-day plan for the content programme.
  6. The catalogue is built by part number, with no page written for the buyer's own search words. Build a page for each system line (intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators, wireless, panels and keypads, Virtual Keypad and software), each with question headings, FAQPage markup and links down to the products. In the build.
  7. The brand reputation result is owned by job boards and Reddit. Publish an about and proof page carrying dealer testimonials, installation case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and every service page. In the 30-day plan.
  8. Nothing on the site answers a question in the words buyers use. Put six to eight questions with direct answers and FAQPage markup at the foot of each of the eight system pages, drawn from the question lists above. In the build for the markup, 30-day plan for the copy.
  9. Pages say little about what they are: short titles, one shared description, thin copy, images without alt text. Generate a descriptive title, a unique description, alt text and 300 or more words from the product table for every product page, and give shared links a product image. In the build.
  10. The category head terms are all unranked, and the reachable ones are being ignored. Point the access control and fire pages at the difficulty 22 to 42 commercial terms and build supporting question pages beneath them. In the 90-day plan.
  11. The backlink total rests on one relationship. Earn links from domains that have none yet, starting with security trade publications, the Springfield chamber and business press, and dealer sites, and ask partners who link with a logo to put the company name in the alt text. In the 90-day plan.
  12. AI crawlers are allowed by accident, not by policy, and llms.txt is not published. Publish a deliberate robots.txt that names and allows the eight crawlers, and an llms.txt listing the home page, the eight system pages, the Springfield page and the support hub. In the build, week one.
  13. No paid search at all, and no paid-sourced contacts in the CRM. Once the service pages exist, run a small brand-defence campaign on the five brand terms and a test on 'access control companies' and 'door access control systems'. In the 90-day plan.

Every number here came from a Semrush or Firecrawl pull, or from the live HTML of www.dmp.com, on 13 September 2026. Where a pull was not made, the table says so. Rankings and traffic are not promised; the inputs are, and they are re-measured against this baseline.
